title: Resilient audit relay: modular sink adapters + customer-managed storage handshake
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Private/VPC/on-prem customers need guaranteed, auditable delivery of account and admin audit events into customer-managed storage (S3-compatible blobstores, GCS, Azure Blob, and air-gapped appliances). Existing shipper prototypes have single-path assumptions (direct signed upload or cloud sink) and lack modular adapters, resumable uploads, ordered delivery guarantees, and a short cryptographic handshake for CMEK/temporary credentials. This ticket defines a resilient relay design with pluggable sink adapters, a CMEK-compatible key handshake for signing uploads, resumable encrypted chunking for unstable networks, RBAC v2 controls for who can configure sinks, and administrative flows for SSO/SAML-protected consoles.
acceptance_criteria: Relay implements adapter interface and has adapters for S3-compatible, GCS, Azure Blob, and local SMB/NFS proxy
Resumable, checkpointed multipart upload protocol survives restarts and network blips without data loss
At-least-once delivery with idempotency keys and event sequence watermarking to preserve ordering semantics for audit consumers
Admin UI exposes RBAC v2 controls: only users in Auditor or InfraAdmin roles can create/rotate sinks; changes require SSO-backed 2FA for high-privilege tenants
CMEK handshake implemented: short-lived envelope keys retrieved via customer KMS integrations (KMS/HSM) and never persisted in plaintext
End-to-end encryption in transit and at-rest in customer store; documented threat model and tests
Automated integration tests that run against a local S3-compatible emulator and a GCS emulator in CI
Security review completed and compliance checklist signed off for Private deployments
Migration/upgrade plan for existing customers using legacy shipper without breaking delivery
design_notes: Core idea: split the shipper into two logical components - Relay Core (stateful, checkpointed uploader) and Adapter Layer (stateless connectors to storage). Relay Core maintains an append-only local journal of batched audit records (encrypted) and a visibility state machine (queued, uploading, verifying, failed). Adapters implement a deterministic upload handshake and mapping to destination semantics (multipart, single blob, object composition). Use per-tenant monotonic sequence IDs + per-batch UUIDs so idempotency is possible. For CMEK, implement an ephemeral envelope key flow: Relay requests an envelope key from control plane with a customer-signed nonce; control plane proxies to customer KMS (or issues short-lived signed pre-signed URLs with envelope key encrypted under KMS). For air-gapped customers add a 'disk-transfer' adapter that writes to an encrypted tarball with accompanying checksum and manifest for manual pickup. For RBAC v2, reuse roles schema but add 'audit:configure_sink' and 'audit:rotate_keys' granular permissions; enforce via SSO groups mapping. Keep admin actions audited locally and forwarded as audit events themselves.
implementation_plan: 1) Define adapter interface and publish spec (Go interface + OpenAPI contract for HTTP-based adapter mocks)
2) Implement Relay Core state machine and local encrypted journal (leveldb + AES-GCM per-tenant keys)
3) Build adapters: S3-compatible (minio/ceph), GCS, Azure Blob, SMB/NFS-proxy, disk-transfer for air-gap
4) Implement CMEK handshake path with control-plane proxy endpoints and HSM/KMS integration points (configurable per-deployment)
5) Add RBAC v2 checks in Console and private control plane API for sink creation/rotation; map SAML group attributes to roles
6) Add resumable multipart logic and idempotency keys; persist checkpoints in journal and expose reconciliation API
7) End-to-end integration tests and chaos testing (network partitions, reboot during multipart upload)
8) Docs (runbook, integration guide for customer storage config, security whitepaper)
9) Beta rollout with 3 pilot customers in Dedicated/Private; collect metrics and iterate
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal dogfooding on staging + synthetic load (2 weeks). Phase B: invite 3 pilot customers with dedicated support engineers; collect telemetry and run monthly drills (3 weeks). Phase C: gradual opt-in release to all Dedicated tenants with migration tooling for legacy shipper; opt-out available for 30 days (4 weeks). Phase D: GA for Private and VPC with docs and compliance artifacts (2 weeks). Each phase gated by security review, integration test pass, and SLA benchmarks.
testing_plan: Automated unit tests for adapter shim, integration tests using localstack/minio and gcloud emulator, e2e tests that simulate unstable links and restarts, property tests for idempotency and sequence numbers, CI job with chaos injected via toxiproxy. Include a smoke-check tool that verifies uploaded object manifests and checksums. Add fuzz test for adapter inputs.
security_considerations:
- Threat model attached: Mitigations include envelope encryption via CMEK, not storing customer keys on relay, signing of manifests, mutual TLS for control plane-replay protection, strict RBAC v2 enforcement for sink lifecycle operations.
- Ensure audit events that contain sensitive hashes are redacted before sending to third-party storage unless customer explicitly opts in.
- Replay protection via monotonic sequence IDs and HMAC on batch headers.
- Require SAML SSO + MFA for roles that can configure sinks; provide 'break-glass' emergency flow that is audited and requires support approval.
reviewer_feedback: PM (Lena Ortiz): please call out expected cost delta for pilot customers and whether we can defer disk-transfer adapter until after GA. Security (Daniel Chow): tighten the KMS proxy audit logging and ensure HSM attestation for private installs. Eng (Kofi Mensah): prefer protobuf over JSON for adapter wire format to reduce parsing overhead on high-throughput relays.
